permit.quote: We use information that may be considered Sensitive Personal Information under state laws for each of the purposes described above and may make inferences about customers, which we may use to promote certain products or services.

prohibit.quote: your sensitive personal information may be processed for the purposes disclosed at the time of collection, but it will not be used for the purpose of targeted advertising

conflicts.situation: A US customer consents to processing of sensitive data such as ethnicity or precise location, and Walmart selects data for targeted advertising.
conflicts.reason: The listed purposes include targeted advertising, so one statement permits it for sensitive data and the appendix forbids it. Appendix 1 sits outside the region-specific sections, so the precedence clause does not clearly decide.

permit.quote: such as voice prints, imagery of the iris or retina, face geometry, and palm prints or fingerprints

prohibit.quote: Walmart does not use voice data for biometric analysis.

conflicts.situation: Walmart records a customer's voice, for example in a voice search or customer service call, and derives a voice print from it.
conflicts.reason: The notice lists voice prints as collected biometric information but also denies biometric analysis of voice data. It names no product or source for voice prints that would separate the two statements.

permit.quote: click data, features you use, types of advertisements you interact with, duration of your visit

prohibit.quote: Your interests and interactions with ads are not stored on our servers, but we do benefit from this practice.

conflicts.situation: A user clicks an ad on MediaFire, and MediaFire records the ad interaction as part of the behavior data it gathers and analyzes.
conflicts.reason: One passage lists ad interactions among the behavior data MediaFire gathers and analyzes, while another says ad interactions are not stored on its servers. The policy does not separate first-party logging from the advertisers' data.

permit.quote: If you click on that notification, you will then receive options to either dismiss it or opt-out of the sale of your personal information, in accordance with the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

prohibit.quote: We do not, now or in the past, engage in data mining or selling personal information.

conflicts.situation: A California user's browsing data is passed to MediaFire's third-party advertisers such as Ezoic, and the user sees the Do Not Sell notice.
conflicts.reason: The California notice offers an opt-out of sale, which presupposes that MediaFire sells personal information, while the policy denies any sale. Nothing says whether advertising disclosures count as sales.

permit.quote: When you consent to geolocation tracking on the App we will disclose your geolocation information to third parties.

prohibit.quote: Fetch does not sell or share your sensitive personal information with third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising.

conflicts.situation: A user consents to App geolocation tracking, and Fetch discloses the precise location to third parties listed under the sold-or-shared-for-advertising heading.
conflicts.reason: The geolocation disclosure appears under the heading for data sold or shared for cross-context behavioral advertising, yet precise geolocation is sensitive and stated as never sold or shared. The policy does not say which governs.

permit.quote: General Geolocation Data (excluding precise geolocation, which is not sold or shared)

prohibit.quote: Separate from precise geo-location options, our App when the app is being utilized approximates your device location solely for fraud detection purposes.

conflicts.situation: A user without precise location enabled uses the App; Fetch approximates the device location and discloses general geolocation to analytics providers and advertising partners.
conflicts.reason: The disclosure tables list general geolocation as sold or shared with advertising partners, but the App's approximate location is used only for fraud detection. The policy does not say whether the sold geolocation comes from another source.

permit.quote: We may disclose your information to our brand partners, third-party service providers, and advertising platforms to facilitate the delivery of personalized offers and advertisements.

prohibit.quote: We do not sell or share: other personal information, including sensitive information, other than noted above.

conflicts.situation: Fetch discloses a user's purchase history from scanned receipts to advertising platforms to deliver personalized advertisements.
conflicts.reason: Commercial information appears under the heading for data sold or shared for cross-context behavioral advertising, but the sale table lists only identifiers, network activity, and geolocation and denies selling or sharing anything else.

permit.quote: Parents and legal guardians may choose to provide information about their children, even if under the age of 13, for the purposes of using our products and services, including, without limitation, the App and Website.

prohibit.quote: We do not knowingly collect information of minors under the age of 13.

conflicts.situation: A parent provides their 10-year-old child's information to Fetch to use the App.
conflicts.reason: Accepting a parent's submission of a child's information is knowing collection of information about a minor under 13. The policy states no parental-consent exception to the no-collection statement.
